real_qa.q: What percentage of the web runs on PHP and how many websites are affected?
real_qa.r: An estimated 70% of the web has PHP running underneath it, with approximately 20 million sites that involve PHP at some level. This makes PHP patches critical because a large portion of internet infrastructure depends on it.

real_qa.q: How many malicious messages did the criminal storefronts send in 2026 targeting healthcare?
real_qa.r: Since January 2026, Microsoft estimated that these criminal service storefronts were responsible for putting together 1 billion malicious messages aimed at over 75,000 organizations just in 2026.

real_qa.q: What was the YAM Store criminal operation and how did it obtain legitimate Microsoft 365 accounts?
real_qa.r: The YAM Store was a criminal marketplace that purchased expired domain names from legitimate organizations, then built fraudulent websites impersonating those organizations and obtained real Microsoft 365 accounts under those domain names. This allowed them to bypass security checks since the accounts appeared completely legitimate with established domain history.

real_qa.q: How many domains and accounts were seized in the takedown of these criminal storefronts?
real_qa.r: More than 20,000 accounts were disabled from the YAM Store, and more than 100,000 domains that were being used in these operations were then blocked during the coordinated takedown.

real_qa.q: What is Operation Riptide and what was its focus on healthcare cybercrime?
real_qa.r: Operation Riptide was a 60-day coordinated cybercrime crackdown led by the FBI Cyber Division targeting criminals specifically attacking healthcare organizations. It involved private sector intelligence sharing with the FBI and international organizations working together to disrupt criminal networks and shut down their infrastructure.
